newsitem.title: CHINA: China says firms from nine nations submit dam bids.
newsitem.headline: China says firms from nine nations submit dam bids.

text.p: China said on Saturday that companies from nine countries had submitted bids to supply generators for its Three Gorges dam project by the tender deadline 10 days ago.
The official Xinhua news agency said Siemens AG, ABB, and Mitsubishi of Japan were among those that submitted tender documents. It gave no further details.

It quoted an official of the Three Gorges Project Development Corp, the overseer of the hydroelectric dam project, as saying that companies worldwide were engaged in cutthroat competition to supply the generators.
The agency also said that some consortia bidding on the project had won financial support from their governments.
China was now evaluating the bids which would not be awarded until next summer, it said.
China plans to buy 14 turbine generators, each of 700 megawatts, for the hydroelectric dam on the Yangtze river. It hopes 12 will be mainly foreign built and the other two domestically sourced.
The first generators would start operating in 2003 and the project would be completed in 2009.
